subject: mathematics
question_text: For x, y ∈ R, prove that sinh(x + y) = sinh x cosh y + cosh x sinh y.

mark_split.label: Cancel and read off sinh(x + y)

steps.label: Substitute the definitions
steps.margin_note: First mark. Start from the right side, which has something to expand. Every definition has a 2 below it, so the two products share a denominator of 4.
steps.memory_tip: Each definition has a 2 below, so a product of two of them has 4 below. Work with 4·R.H.S and divide at the end.
lines: R.H.S = sinh x cosh y + cosh x sinh y
Each definition has a 2 below, so take 4·R.H.S

recall.must_convey: That both terms on the right are replaced by their exponential definitions, giving two products over a common denominator of 4.
accept: substitute the exponential definitions for sinh and cosh on the right side
each definition has a two below so the product has four below
write four times the right side as two products of brackets
right side lo definitions substitute chesi four times rasta
replace sinh and cosh by e to the x forms

steps.why: The left side sinh(x + y) is already in its simplest form, so there is nothing to do to it. The right side is the one with two products waiting to be expanded.
common_mistakes: Using a denominator of 2 instead of 4 for a product of two definitions.
Pairing sinh x with sinh y instead of sinh x with cosh y.

steps.label: Cancel and read off sinh(x + y)
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The eˣ⁻ʸ terms and the eʸ⁻ˣ terms have opposite signs in the two brackets, so they cancel and only the x + y terms survive.
steps.memory_tip: The mixed terms eˣ⁻ʸ and eʸ⁻ˣ appear once with a plus and once with a minus, so they cancel in pairs.

recall.must_convey: That the mixed terms cancel in pairs, leaving (eˣ⁺ʸ − e⁻⁽ˣ⁺ʸ⁾)/2, which is sinh(x + y).
accept: the mixed terms cancel and only the x plus y terms are left
two e to the x plus y minus two e to the minus x plus y over four
what remains is e to the x plus y minus e to the minus x plus y over two which is sinh x plus y
middle terms cancel ayi sinh x plus y vasthundi
the result is sinh of x plus y

steps.why: Reading (eˣ⁺ʸ − e⁻⁽ˣ⁺ʸ⁾)/2 back as sinh(x + y) is the definition used in reverse, with x + y in the place of the single variable.
common_mistakes: Losing a sign on eʸ⁻ˣ, so the mixed terms fail to cancel.
Dividing by 2 instead of 4 when going back from 4·R.H.S.
